newsitem.title: LEBANON: Banque Audi Eurobond heavily oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: Banque Audi Eurobond heavily oversubscribed.

text.p: Banque Audi's $100 million Eurobond launched on Wednesday was heavily oversubscribed and sold strongly to institutional investors overseas, market sources in Beirut said.
Demand totalled more than $250 million, the sources said, and the issue was increased to $100 million from an initial indicated size of $75 million.
It was placed 75 percent with institutional investors and sold 40 percent in the United States, 40 percent in Europe and 20 percent in the Middle East, the sources added.
"This is the first Lebanese institution to tap into the real institutional investors," they said.
Banque Audi is the fifth Lebanese commercial bank to tap into the international debt market. The previous issues have totalled some $220 million since June.
The five-year issue launches Audi's $200 million Euronote programme lead managed by Merrill Lynch International, a Merrill Lynch said.
The issue was priced at 99.824 with a coupon of 9.375 percent to yield 315 basis points over the corresponding five-year U.S. Treasury Notes, it said.
Merrill Lynch said it marked a number of precedents for the region, including:
- the first five-year issue by a private sector Lebanese borrower,
- the first Lebanese issue marketed and sold into the United States through a 144A tranche,
- the first Euro-medium term note (EMTN) programme established by a Lebanese or Arab issuer, and
- the first London Stock Exchange listing for a Middle Eastern issuer.
Market sources said the bonds would be listed on the London Stock Exchange after closing, expected November 5.
